topic: Kubernetes resource requests and limits — syntax and examples
linkedin_hook: Mastering Kubernetes resource management is crucial for optimizing your cluster's performance and efficiency, and I'm excited to share my top cheatsheet with you!
linkedin_intro: As a senior DevOps engineer, I've worked with numerous teams to optimize their Kubernetes deployments, and I've compiled a list of essential commands and configurations to help you get started. In this cheatsheet, I'll share my expertise on Kubernetes resource requests and limits, including syntax and examples. Whether you're a beginner or an experienced engineer, this guide will help you streamline your workflow and improve your cluster's overall performance.

pro_tips:
Use the `kubectl top` command to monitor resource usage and identify bottlenecks in your cluster
Configure resource requests and limits for your containers to ensure efficient resource allocation and prevent overcommitting
Implement horizontal pod autoscaling to dynamically adjust the number of replicas based on resource usage and other metrics
Use the `kubectl patch` command to update resource requests and limits for existing resources, rather than recreating them from scratch
